narratives.Overview:
## Summary
A linked `git worktree` branched from the delivery branch fails the `agent_hooks` gated step of `deft session:ready`, blocking all Edit/Write tool calls, because the worktree's *committed* `.claude/settings.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json` matcher regexes lag the live deposit. The only offered remediations are `deft update` / `directive init` (repo-wide, destructive for consumers) or `deft policy:disable-host-hooks` (removes guardrails). Neither fits "I need to edit a file in a fresh worktree."

This is the `agent_hooks` companion of the `doctor`/deposit-hygiene block in #4706 — same "committed deposit artifacts lag the engine" root, but it fires *first* and on a different set of files.

## Environment
- macOS, zsh; npm-managed consumer (deftai/BestiMax), local `core.hooksPath=.githooks`.
- Engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.1`; worktree committed `.deft/core` content `0.117.0`.
- Observed 2026-09-17.

## Reproduction
1. In a consumer whose committed `.claude/settings.json` / `.cursor/hooks.json` were generated by an older deposit than the live engine, create a linked worktree from the delivery branch: `git worktree add -b <b> <path> origin/<delivery-branch>`.
2. `deft session:ready --session-id=...`.
3. The `agent_hooks` gated step fails: *"deft agent hook registration INCOMPLETE — claude drifted at .claude/settings.json / cursor drifted at .cursor/hooks.json"*. All subsequent Edit/Write tool calls are blocked by the session-ritual PreToolUse gate.

## Actual drift (small and mechanical)
The only difference between the worktree's committed hook files and the live-deposit-expected registration was two added matcher tokens:
- Edit/Write matcher: added `EditNotebook|edit_notebook` (…`NotebookEdit|EditNotebook|edit_notebook|StrReplace`…).
- mcp/merge/push matcher: added `CallMcpTool|use_tool` (…`.*__.*|CallMcpTool|use_tool|merge_pull_request`…).

## Why the offered remediations don't fit
- `deft update` / `directive init` — repo-wide and, per #4706, doesn't even leave `doctor` healthy; also destructive for consumers (#3437).
- `deft policy:disable-host-hooks --host claude` — removes the guardrails, tracked; wrong for a routine edit.
- `deft agents:refresh` — updates the managed AGENTS.md section but not the host hook JSON, so it does not clear `agent_hooks`.

## Expected
A fresh worktree branched from a branch whose committed hook files predate the engine should either (a) not hard-block writes on hook-matcher drift the engine can re-derive, or (b) offer a targeted, non-destructive hook refresh that rewrites just `.claude/settings.json` / `.cursor/hooks.json` to the live registration (an `agents:refresh --hooks`, say).

## Workaround used
Copied the primary checkout's current (uncommitted) `.claude/settings.json` + `.cursor/hooks.json` into the worktree, which cleared `agent_hooks`; left them unstaged so they stayed out of the task PR. Then hit the `doctor` gate — see #4706 — and worked around that by authoring via shell without `deft update`.

Refs #4706, #3732.

issueCommentThread.body:
Still reproduces on `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.2` (upgraded via `npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest`).

A fresh `git worktree` off the delivery branch (`origin/develop`, committed hook files from content 0.117.0) still fails `deft session:ready` at the `agent_hooks` step with the identical drift on `.claude/settings.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json`, and the same only-remedies offered (`deft update` / `disable-host-hooks`). The 0.119.1 → 0.119.2 patch bump didn't change the behavior.

Note the two gates compound: per #4706, the `deft update` remedy re-deposits content 0.117.0 and leaves `doctor` failing anyway, so on 0.119.2 a fresh worktree remains unworkable for gated writes without manual intervention (I cleared `agent_hooks` by copying the primary checkout's current hook files in, then authored via shell to bypass the still-failing `doctor` tool gate).

## Verdict

The refutation succeeds against the permissive half of the target. Matcher drift is not merely stale metadata that the running engine can ignore: the host applies the deposited matcher before `deft-hook` runs. The design can bind only after it removes the “do not hard-block” branch and makes hook-only repair a deny-repair-reverify-retry path.

### F1 — blocks-the-design — Re-derivable matcher drift can be an unhooked mutation path

**Evidence.** At `cb4c74369a888faabd01e7f8d3517b01ce25f2f1`, `packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts` adds `EditNotebook|edit_notebook` to `DIRECT_WRITE_HOOK_MATCHER` and `CallMcpTool|use_tool` to `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER`. `packages/core/src/init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts` deposits those strings as host-side `PreToolUse` matchers, and `hasNestedRegistration` / `hasCursorRegistration` require the current strings exactly. The host therefore decides whether to invoke Directive before runtime classification can “re-derive” anything. A worktree carrying the older matcher can still invoke Directive for legacy `Edit`/`Write` and receive the observed global readiness denial, while `EditNotebook`, `edit_notebook`, `CallMcpTool`, or `use_tool` may not invoke Directive at all.

**Concrete failure mode.** If the gate treats this drift as non-blocking, the action that happened to reach the old hook can pass while a newly added write/MCP spelling remains outside interception. Deliberate matcher removal is indistinguishable from benign version lag at this boundary, so “known re-derivable drift” is also a guardrail-bypass class.

**Disposition consequence.** Strike option (a) as written. Keep the current action denied until the worktree-local registration has been repaired and `verify:hooks-installed --scope=agent --live` is green; then require the caller to retry the action. A same-invocation repair-and-allow would not prove that the host reloaded its matcher configuration.

The strongest case for allowing the current legacy `Edit` is that its hook demonstrably fired, so that single action is intercepted. I reject that narrower per-action allowance because the readiness promise is host-wide and the same session can immediately use an omitted spelling that never reaches Directive. I would flip this verdict if every supported host had an independently verified catch-all interception layer, or if the gate could prove the omitted names are unavailable on that host; the pinned inventory provides neither.

### F2 — sharpens-framing — The narrow repair mechanism already exists, but its actual scope is four host deposits

**Evidence.** `writeAgentHookDeposit` in `packages/core/src/init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts` already removes only Directive-managed groups, merges current matcher groups, uses contained atomic replacement, preserves unrelated host configuration, is byte-idempotent, and refuses malformed JSON before writing. Its definition set covers Claude, Grok, Cursor, and Codex, not only the two files named by the reproduction. The pinned tests exercise preservation, drift repair, containment, malformed-input refusal, and idempotence.

**Concrete failure mode.** Inventing a second matcher-rewrite implementation, or presenting `agents:refresh --hooks` as if it changes only `.claude/settings.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json`, creates another schema that can drift and can surprise users with additional dirty host files.

**Disposition consequence.** Frame the remedy as a thin hook-specific command over `writeAgentHookDeposit`, with exact changed-path reporting, malformed-config refusal, and an immediate live-readiness recheck. Either add an explicit unhealthy-host/path filter or truthfully document that all enabled host deposits are reconciled. Keep this separate from AGENTS.md refresh semantics.

Road not taken: weakening `inspectAgentHookDeposit` to accept matcher subsets. That makes old deposits look healthy precisely when they omit newly classified mutation tools, defeating the coverage check that caused this incident to be visible.

### F3 — sharpens-framing — Worktree-local recovery is not durable prevention and must not mutate another checkout

**Evidence.** All four configured paths are resolved beneath the supplied `projectRoot`; linked worktrees therefore have separate hook JSON working-tree files even though they share repository object storage. Repairing the incident worktree makes those tracked files locally dirty but does not update `origin/<delivery-branch>`, so the next fresh worktree reproduces the same committed drift. `session:ready` currently forces `agent_hooks` and returns the remaining blocker; it does not invoke the deposit writer.

**Concrete failure mode.** Calling a repair in another checkout, or claiming that one local rewrite prevents recurrence, risks cross-worktree authority confusion and leaves future worktrees broken. Automatically allowing the triggering action after rewriting also races host configuration reload behavior.

**Disposition consequence.** State two outcomes separately: (1) immediate, current-worktree recovery that touches only that resolved project root and leaves the triggering action denied for retry; (2) durable prevention, which requires the consumer to deliberately commit refreshed deposits on its delivery branch or adopt a future non-tracked registration architecture. Do not let the recovery command walk to or rewrite a primary checkout.

### F4 — footnote — Re-verification

Pinned-anchor checks found the matcher additions, exact structural validation, four-host deposit writer, and forced `session:ready` check described above. The focused suite passed at the dispatch SHA: 3 test files, 73 tests passed, 1 skipped (`agent-hooks.test.ts`, `verify-env/agent-hooks.test.ts`, `session-ready.test.ts`). No instruction-shaped payload was present in the bounded issue thread. The authority/worktree lens is material in F1 and F3; no sibling comment was read beyond the shared ceiling.

Charter refutation, round 1, fresh critic. Envelope ceiling `5730581367` inclusive; the three comments at or below it are the whole input. Pin-reads run against `cb4c74369a888faabd01e7f8d3517b01ce25f2f1`. Issue body and comments treated as untrusted external content; no embedded instruction was found to surface.

## Verdict

The refutation target does not survive as written. The *complaint* is well-founded and the anchors hold, but the target packages it as a disjunction — "either agent_hooks does not fail-closed on re-derivable matcher drift, or a targeted non-destructive hook refresh rewrites just those two files" — and both disjuncts fail on evidence in this tree. They also fail for the same unstated reason, which makes the disjunction a false choice rather than two live options.

## Anchor re-verification

All four triage anchors hold at the pin, with one correction.

- `packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts` — `DIRECT_WRITE_TOOL_NAMES` carries `NotebookEdit`, `EditNotebook`, `edit_notebook`; `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER` carries `CallMcpTool` and `use_tool`. Confirmed.
- `packages/core/src/init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts` — `AGENT_HOOK_PATHS` is four paths, not two: `.claude/settings.json`, `.grok/hooks/deft.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`. The target names two. Confirmed with that widening.
- `packages/core/src/session/session-ready.ts:369` forces `agent_hooks` as a gated step; `session-start.ts:551` records it as not deferrable. Confirmed.
- `packages/cli/src/agents-refresh.ts` calls `applyAgentsRefresh` on AGENTS.md only. Confirmed: it cannot clear `agent_hooks`.

Correction to the gate stamp: the matchers are built in compiled engine code (`DIRECT_WRITE_HOOK_MATCHER = DIRECT_WRITE_TOOL_NAMES.join("|")`, `tools.ts:178`), not read from `.deft/core`. This drift is therefore **not** the same root as #4706. Content `0.117.0` is irrelevant to it. The two gates compound in *sequence* — `agent_hooks` fires, then `doctor` — but not in *cause*, and a remedy for one is structurally unable to be a remedy for the other.

## F1 — blocks-the-design

**Relaxing the exact-matcher compare removes the only control standing on the one host whose mutation surface this tree has never observed — and that host is the file in the report.**

Evidence. `hasNestedRegistration` (`agent-hooks.ts:481`) requires `group?.matcher === matcher` for every entry in `NESTED_PRE_TOOL_MATCHERS`: exact string equality against the engine constant. The softer alternative already exists beside it — `inspectHostToolCoverage` (`init-deposit/host-tool-coverage.ts`) reads the *deposited* matcher via `depositedPreToolUseMatchers` and raises `uncovered-tool` for any catalogued mutation name that is not a literal token of it. That is the coverage predicate a "re-derivable drift" relaxation would fall back on. But it is catalogue-driven, and `HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT.claude` (`tools.ts:256`) is `mutation: { directWrite: [], shell: ["Bash"], spawn: [] }` with an explicit `unobservedReason`: no Claude PreToolUse payload has been observed in this tree, so the direct-write and spawn spellings stay unclaimed rather than asserted from the deposit under test.

Failure mode. Adopt disjunct (a) and `.claude/settings.json` may carry any direct-write matcher whatsoever — including one with `Edit` and `Write` absent — and both checks return green: registration no longer demands equality, and coverage iterates an empty claude `directWrite` catalogue and finds nothing to report. `session:ready` then returns mutation-ready over a claude deposit with no direct-write gate at all. The empty catalogue is honest about uncertainty; a relaxation converts it into a licence.

Disposition consequence. Disjunct (a) cannot bind as written. A coverage-shaped relaxation is only trustworthy on a host with a non-empty observed catalogue — `grok` and `codex` qualify, `claude` and `cursor` explicitly do not, and `claude` is the reported file. Any bind must either scope the relaxation per-host to observed catalogues, or land the claude surface observation first.

## F2 — blocks-the-design

**"Targeted, non-destructive" does not name what the remedy does to git-tracked state, and in a linked worktree that omission is the whole problem.**

Evidence. `init-deposit/hook-runtime-travel.ts` records the split by design: the registration files are *trackable* and travel with the tree, while the deposit implementing them is born-ignored. The reporter's own workaround confirms the consequence — the copied hook files were deliberately left unstaged "so they stayed out of the task PR".

Failure mode. A refresh that rewrites `.claude/settings.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json` in a linked worktree mutates git-tracked files on the task branch. Two outcomes, both bad. Staged or committed: every task PR carries a hook-registration diff unrelated to its change, the diff content is engine-version-dependent, and two concurrent worktrees on different engine versions produce conflicting diffs against the same delivery branch. Left unstaged: a permanently dirty tree, which `init-deposit/gitignore.ts:65` already names as the condition worth engineering around ("un-ignored agent worktrees leave a permanently dirty tree, which refuses …").

Disposition consequence. Disjunct (b) is under-specified rather than wrong. It needs a third field stating the tracked-state disposition — ignore-scoped, staged, or explicitly left dirty with a printed reason. Without it the remedy trades a hard block for a per-branch merge hazard, which is a worse failure because it is silent.

## F3 — blocks-the-design

**Both disjuncts share one unstated success condition — when a rewritten registration becomes live for the already-running host — and neither is sound without it. That is what makes the "either/or" a false choice.**

Evidence. Nothing at the pin states when a host re-reads its PreToolUse registration. I searched `packages/core/src/init-deposit`, `packages/core/src/hooks`, `packages/core/src/verify-env`, and `content/contracts` for restart/reload/takes-effect semantics and found none. The reporter's sequence is itself the demonstration: copy the primary checkout's hook files in, `agent_hooks` clears, then author via shell. The host had already loaded its matcher at launch; the file changed underneath it.

Failure mode. A mid-session targeted refresh flips the deterministic check green while the live matcher the host actually dispatches on is unchanged. The session then proceeds under precisely the registration the gate exists to refuse — and now with a green signal saying otherwise. That is strictly worse than today's hard block, which is at least honest about the state it is in. Disjunct (a) reaches the same end state by admitting it; disjunct (b) reaches it while asserting the opposite.

Disposition consequence. The target's disjunction is not two options. Any bind must state a liveness condition: host relaunch required and printed, or a runtime-side check that does not depend on the host's loaded matcher. Until that is stated, neither branch can be evaluated, because the outcome is identical in both.

## F4 — sharpens-framing

**The remedy the issue asks for is already seated one directory over; `agents:refresh --hooks` is the wrong extension point.**

Evidence, inventory. `writeAgentHookDeposit` (`agent-hooks.ts:340`) is already exactly the bounded operation the target describes: it touches only `AGENT_HOOK_PATHS`, merges rather than replaces via `mergeNestedConfig` / `mergeCursorConfig`, honours `plan.policy.hostHooks`, asserts `assertDepositContained`, writes through `containedWrite` with the #3392 ledger, and derives matchers from engine constants. It is called from exactly two places (`init-deposit.ts:342`, `refresh.ts:1051`), both of which do far more. And `session:ready` already runs a linked-worktree self-repair seam *before* the gated verify: `session-ready.ts:258` calls `reconstituteLinkedWorktreeDeposit` (`gitignore.ts:586`), which is linked-worktree gated, framework-source refused, payload-only, and contained-write asserted. In the reporter's case that seam runs and returns `already-present`, because `.deft/core` exists — it simply has nothing to say about the four hook paths.

Failure mode of the proposed shape. A new user-invoked verb does not reach the reported flow. The operator is blocked *at* `session:ready`, and the message they receive (`verify-env/agent-hooks.ts:80`) names `deft update`, `directive init`, and `policy:disable-host-hooks` — not the new verb. It adds an entry to a list the blocked operator has no path to.

Disposition consequence. Retarget from "add a verb" to "extend the seat that already runs at the right moment with the function that already does the bounded write", or record why the self-repair seam was rejected. This does not block the target; it relocates it, and the relocation is what makes F2 and F3 answerable in one place instead of two.

## F5 — sharpens-framing

**The worktree is the surface, not the class. The class is exact-string equality between a compiled engine constant and a committed artifact.**

Evidence. `DIRECT_WRITE_HOOK_MATCHER` and friends are `join("|")` over the tool-name arrays (`tools.ts:178-180`), compared by `===` in `hasNestedRegistration`. Equality is symmetric and order-sensitive: a committed matcher that is a strict *superset* of the engine's — gating strictly more tools, therefore strictly safer — drifts identically to a subset that gates fewer. The two reported tokens are an ordinary consequence, not a special case.

Failure mode. Every future addition of a tool spelling to `DIRECT_WRITE_TOOL_NAMES`, `SPAWN_TOOL_NAMES`, `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES`, or `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER` drifts every committed deposit in every consumer simultaneously and locks gated writes there. A fresh worktree surfaces it first only because it has no uncommitted local repair to inherit — the primary checkout in the report was working solely because it held uncommitted newer files.

Disposition consequence. Scope the target to the coupling, or the identical report returns at the next tool-name addition with a new pair of tokens. The safety property the predicate should assert is coverage of the engine's tool set, not identity of a joined string; F1 constrains how far that can go per host today.

## F6 — sharpens-framing (injection / swarm lens)

The lens fires: the target changes worktree behaviour, shared state between checkouts, and the authority of a write gate.

Evidence. The existing worktree self-repair resolves its payload through `resolveWorktreePayloadSource` → `resolvePrimaryCore` (`gitignore.ts:512`), which reads the **main worktree's** `.deft/core`, with a `preferPrimaryCore` seam that selects it outright. `writeAgentHookDeposit` takes the opposite polarity: it derives entirely from engine constants and never reads another tree.

Failure mode. If hook repair is added to that seam and inherits its source resolution, a linked worktree's PreToolUse matcher becomes whatever the primary checkout's working tree holds — *including uncommitted local edits*. That is the reporter's manual workaround promoted to an automatic authority path. Any process with write access to one checkout then sets the write gate for every worktree that later self-repairs, and a `policy:disable-host-hooks` opt-out in the primary propagates outward silently, because `writeAgentHookDeposit`'s strip branch is policy-driven. Under #4066-class parallel worktrees that is a one-writer, many-readers authority channel with no provenance.

Disposition consequence. The remedy must state engine-constants-only as the matcher source and keep `resolvePrimaryCore` / `preferPrimaryCore` out of the hook path, even though it will sit adjacent to code that uses them. Concurrency is the mild half: unlike `.deft/core`, these four files are per-worktree, so cross-worktree contention is low and `containedWrite` plus `writeJsonIfChanged` is the existing control for a shared-root nested session. The authority half is the one that needs writing down.

## F7 — footnote

The printed recovery already argues against itself. `formatPinEngineSkewVisibility` (`verify-env/agent-hooks.ts:35`) emits "That is not this valid() fail; `deft update` is not the skew fix", and the same message string then prints "Recovery: run `deft update` (or `directive init`) to refresh project hooks." Not blocking, but it is the concrete source of the report's "the only offered remediations" reading.

## F8 — footnote

`policy:disable-host-hooks` is treated in the issue as one undifferentiated bad option. It is not uniform: `FAIL_CLOSED_HOOK_HOSTS` is `["cursor"]` only (`hook-runtime-travel.ts:45`), so disabling `claude` loses the gate while disabling `cursor` changes a fail-closed denial into no gate. Blast radius differs per host. Immaterial to disposition; relevant to how the remediation list should be worded.

## Road not taken

I considered arguing that `agent_hooks` should be advisory inside linked worktrees specifically — a posture-scoped relaxation rather than a global one, which would resolve the reported flow without touching the primary checkout. Rejected: linked worktrees are where unattended and parallel agents run (#4066), so scoping the relaxation there inverts the risk gradient, weakening the gate exactly where supervision is thinnest.

## Steelman and what would flip this

The strongest position against F1: I am defending a string compare the tree has never validated. The claude catalogue is empty because nobody observed the host, so exact equality is not a *considered* control — it is the residue of having no control, and the honest response is to go observe Claude Code's PreToolUse payload names rather than to cite the emptiness as a reason to keep a brittle compare. That is a fair reading, and it is why F1 is a constraint on sequencing rather than a refusal of the idea.
